newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Grandfather Frost, Santa hold Kremlin "summit".
newsitem.headline: Grandfather Frost, Santa hold Kremlin "summit".

text.p: Santa Claus flew in from Lapland for a historic "summit" meeting with Russia's Grandfather Frost in the Kremlin on Tuesday, Orthodox Christmas day, and agreed to set up a "hot line" for future East-West contacts.
Hundreds of excited children gathered in the Kremlin Palace near Red Square to be entertained by the two bearded characters.
Santa wore his traditional red cloak while Grandfather Frost, his Russian counterpart, was accompanied by his granddaughter and helper Snegurochka, the Snow Maiden.
"I hope we can together spread the Christmas spirit not only at Christmas time in both our cultures but also between Christmases and really every day of the year," Santa told a joint news conference.
Santa has said his first ever three-day visit to Russia would "put the final icing on the cake of East-West relations".
He and Grandfather Frost signed a communique on strengthening cooperation for the good of all the world's children.

Finland, once part of the Russian empire and Moscow's foe before and during World War Two, hosts some 400,000 visitors to Santa's Arctic home in Lapland every year and claims to be home to the "real" Father Christmas.

Soviet communists got rid of Christmas as part of their repression of religion and Grandfather Frost became associated with New Year. But he is once more becoming more linked to the religious festival as the Orthodox Church reasserts itself.
Russia's Christmas day, which according to the Orthodox calendar falls on January 7, was declared an official holiday in 1992, a year after the collapse of communism.
